title: Group Anagrams
statement:
Partition a list of words into groups so that every group holds exactly the words that are anagrams of one another.

Contract
- `words` is non-null, may be empty, and may contain duplicates. Each word is non-null and
  made only of lowercase letters `a`-`z`; a word may be empty (empty words are anagrams of each other).
- Return a list of groups. Every input word appears exactly once in exactly one group (duplicates
  stay as separate entries), and two words share a group if and only if they are anagrams.
- Group order and the order of words inside a group do not matter. Do not mutate `words`.

Examples
- `groupAnagrams(List.of("stop", "pots", "cat", "tops", "act"))` returns the groups `[stop, pots, tops]` and `[cat, act]` in any order.
- `groupAnagrams(List.of("", ""))` returns one group `["", ""]`.
- `groupAnagrams(List.of("abc"))` returns one group `[abc]`.

examples.output: [stop, pots, tops] and [cat, act], in any order

hints: Two words are anagrams exactly when they have the same multiset of letters, so look for a representation of that multiset that is identical for all anagrams.
Sorting a word's letters, or counting each of the 26 letters, gives a canonical key. Collect words into a map from key to list.

Build the key from a letter-count signature so each word costs time proportional to its own length, then return the map's values. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of words and each word has bounded length.
inputSyntax: Input: lowercase words separated by commas with no spaces, for example: stop,pots,cat,tops,act
